newsitem.title: USA: HP says may eye other Internet acquisitions.
newsitem.headline: HP says may eye other Internet acquisitions.

text.p: Hewlett-Packard Co Executive Vice President Rick Belluzzo said the Internet has been a central part of the company's strategy and pursuit of it could eventually lead to further acquisitions in the area.
Belluzzo, speaking in a conference call with analysts and reporters, said HP hopes to close its roughly $1.18 billion acquisition of VeriFone Inc by midsummer.

VeriFone Chairman and CEO Hatim Tyabji said in the call that he expected the deal to enable the two companies to "sharply accelerate the evolution and acceptance of electronic commerce," such as Internet and smart card transactions.

Tyabji said the merger would combine VeriFone's lead as a pioneer of electronic payment systems with "a formidible array of technologies" that HP has in the electronic commerce area, including chip cards, personal computers and other systems.

Major implementations of VeriFone for top financial sector customers are already running on HP systems, including BankAmerica Corp, he said, and HP offers a broad distribution outside the financial and merchandising industries where VeriFone has concentrated since it was founded in 1981.
The commpanies also have partnerships with companies like Microsoft Corp, Netscape Communications Corp and Oracle Corp, the executives noted.
Belluzzo said the acquisition underscored the company's goal of being a major player in the Internet market.

"We have made the Internet a central part of our strategy for quite some time," he said in response to an analyst's quesiton. "We are aggressively pursuing that vision; if that involves acquisitions down the road, so be it."
By mid-afternoon HP shares were off one at 49-1/2 and VeriFone shares soared 17-5/8 to 47-3/4.
The VeriFone price reflects HP's one-for-one stock swap merger offer for the company in an acquisition which it intends to account for as a pooling of interests.

The executives declined to discuss details of valuation or any required governmental or antitrust approvals, although the companies said in a statement the deal is subject to approval of VeriFone shareholders, among other things.

"The timing is mostly driven by the speed and the way we want to get things done," said Belluzzo, in a reference to the speed at which businesses develop and expand in the rapidly growing Internet sector.
"Payments is everything in electronic commerce," he said, adding the companies would be forced to be selective in setting strategy because the overall opportunity was so broad.
Tyabji said the two companies work in a similar fashion.
"We looked at working with Hewlett-Packard, qualitively and quantitatively, and feel it's the most optimum method for us to go forward to translate our dreams into reality," he said.

Tyabji said VeriFone's "focus in the financial services sector, together with HP's already existing and formidible distribution infrastructure, we believe will enable us to penetrate markets faster and in a more cohesive manner than we might have been able to do on our own."

VeriFone will continue to build its traditional business, he said. It has a dominant position in the electronic payment delivery market, with its systems handling an estimated $520 billion of the more than $800 billion of electronic transactions in the United States alone last year. Analysts
said the deal will be slightly dilutive to HP's earnings this year and next. HP declined comment on this, citing its upcoming quarterly earnings report due in mid-May.
